results.title: Hetzner Price Increase 2026: All Three Waves Explained
results.author: Capital, Compute
highlights:
Hetzner raised prices three separate times in 2026, and published a percentage for none of them. What it did publish, on the largest of the three, is a full before-and-after price table, which is more useful: it lets anyone compute the real change per plan rather than repeat a headline. Doing that arithmetic produces the finding that explains the whole year. In the adjustment effective 15 June 2026, Hetzner Arm-based CAX plans rose about 31 to 33 percent while its x86 CPX and CCX plans rose between 94 and 192 percent, on the same day, in the same data centres. The spread between those two numbers is the memory shortage, isolated.

...

- → Three waves in 2026: a broad adjustment effective 1 April (announced 23 February), a dedicated-server setup fee adjustment on 29 April, and a standardisation plus price adjustment effective 15 June 2026 at 08:00 CEST.
- → Hetzner published no percentages in any of the three announcements. Every percentage in this article is computed here from the before-and-after price table Hetzner published for the June change.
- → The June change applies to new orders and rescales only. Existing server contracts keep their terms and conditions.
- → Arm CAX plans rose about a third. x86 CPX and CCX plans rose two to six times that, with the steepest move on CPX11 in the USA at roughly 192 percent.
- → Hetzner names the cause directly, citing the massive increase in procurement costs and, in its April setup-fee statement, RAM and NVMe SSDs specifically.

...

The first came with a statement dated 23 February 2026, effective 1 April, saying that the costs to operate its infrastructure and to buy new hardware had both increased dramatically. Hetzner said it had tried hard to optimise costs and prevent increasing prices for as long as possible, but could no longer compensate for the strain. That statement gives no percentages and no per-product breakdown.

The second, on 29 April, was narrower and is easy to miss because it is not a rate change at all. Hetzner adjusted one-off setup fees for dedicated servers, saying that the actual costs of deploying new systems were once again exceeding its previous estimates and could not be meaningfully spread over the contract term. This is the announcement that names the components outright: prices for key hardware components such as RAM and NVMe SSDs have continued to rise.

The third and largest was announced on 27 May and took effect at 08:00 CEST on 15 June 2026. Hetzner framed it as a standardisation of its dedicated server product structure alongside a price adjustment. It covers all dedicated servers and cloud plans at all locations. Web hosting, managed servers, Server Auction machines, IPs, storage products, Load Balancers, Volumes, Snapshots and Object Storage were not affected. Setup fees for most dedicated servers were reduced in the same change, while monthly prices rose.

...

Hetzner published old and new hourly prices in euros for its cloud plans across Germany and Finland, the USA, and Singapore. Computing the change for each gives the following.

Hetzner cloud plan price changes, 15 June 2026, derived from the published price table

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| CPX11 (x86, USA) | +191.7% |
| CCX13 (x86, DE and FI) | +169.1% |
| CCX13 (x86, USA) | +156.2% |
| CPX22 (x86, DE and FI) | +143.7% |
| CCX43 (x86, DE and FI) | +120.8% |
| CCX13 (x86, Singapore) | +96.1% |
| CPX12 (x86, Singapore) | +93.7% |
| CAX11 (Arm, DE and FI) | +33.3% |
| CAX21 (Arm, DE and FI) | +31.2% |

Percentage change per cloud plan on 15 June 2026, computed from the before-and-after hourly euro prices Hetzner published. The two highlighted rows are the Arm-based CAX plans. Every other row is x86. Hetzner publishes the prices but not these percentages.

...

Not automatically, and this is the single most misunderstood part of the June change. Hetzner stated that existing server contracts keep their terms and conditions and remain active, and that the changes apply exclusively to new orders and rescales of existing servers, plus future products on the new structure.

...

If you resize a cloud server, you move onto current pricing. A machine left alone stays on its original contract. So the practical advice for anyone holding pre-June Hetzner capacity is to think carefully before rescaling, because a resize is repricing, and on the x86 lines that can mean close to a tripling rather than an incremental change.

...

There were three dates. A broad adjustment effective 1 April 2026, announced 23 February. A dedicated server setup fee adjustment announced 29 April. And the largest, a standardisation and price adjustment effective 15 June 2026 at 08:00 CEST, announced on 27 May.

# EU GPU Price Index, October 2026: H100, H200 and B200 per hour

...

October 2026 Updated 2 October 2026 By Rogier Muller 

 In October 2026, EU-headquartered cloud providers list an NVIDIA H100 at €2.80 to €3.95 per GPU hour on demand. The US hyperscalers charge €6.03 (AWS), €6.12 (Azure) and €9.70 (Google Cloud). Nebius raised its on-demand GPU prices on 1 October 2026. All figures are published list prices, accessed 1 October 2026, with the source per row.

...

1. EU-headquartered providers rent an H100 for €2.80 to €3.95 an hour, about half the AWS and Azure price.
2. Prices rose. Nebius added 17 to 21 percent on 1 October; Scaleway and Verda added 1 to 5 percent.
3. US specialist clouds such as RunPod and Lambda charge about what European providers charge.

...

results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

...

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

...

H100: At $4.50, Nebius moves above Runpod ($3.49), Crusoe ($3.90) and Lambda ($4.29). It stays below CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance, about $6.16 per GPU.

H200: At $5.40, Nebius moves above Runpod ($4.59) and Verda ($4.55). It stays below Together AI ($5.99) and CoreWeave (about $6.31 per GPU).

B200: At $8.50, Nebius moves well above Lambda ($6.69) and Runpod ($6.79). CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance works out to about $8.60 per GPU.

B300: At $9.50, Nebius moves above Verda ($8.20) and Scaleway ($7.50). Together AI lists $9.99.

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

...

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

results.title: Algo Hosting VPS Costs Surge as AI Demand Hits Trading Infrastructure - Financial Investor 24
results.author: Publishing Wizard
highlights:
Hetzner raised the monthly price of its CPX22 cloud server in Germany and Finland from EUR 7.99 to EUR 19.49 on 15 June 2026, a rise of 143.9%. That change applies to new orders and to existing servers that customers rescale; instances left unchanged retain their previous pricing, according to Hetzner’s official price-adjustment documentation.

The CPX22 increase is not the steepest in Hetzner’s June round. Its dedicated-vCPU CCX13 rose from EUR 15.99 to EUR 42.99, a 169% increase, and the CCX23 climbed from EUR 31.49 to EUR 85.99, up 173%, both on the same new-orders-only basis, according to WZ-IT’s analysis of the June 2026 CPX/CCX changes. Heise Online attributed the move to “still extremely high procurement costs for new hardware.” This was not Hetzner’s first increase in 2026: an earlier round on 1 April 2026 had already raised cloud prices by up to 37% in Germany and Finland, and that earlier round did affect existing customers, per Webhosting.today’s review of Hetzner’s 2026 price rounds.

results.title: European GPU Clouds: 8 Alternatives to AWS and Azure for AI Workloads - Qovery Blog
results.author: Mélanie Dallé
highlights:
- Scaleway (France, Iliad group): H100 PCIe, H100 SXM, L40S and L4 behind managed Kubernetes (Kapsule) with public per-hour pricing. Best for EU teams that want a full cloud and GPUs in one console.
- OVHcloud (France): H100, A100, L40S single cards plus 8xH200 nodes, managed Kubernetes (MKS), free egress and public pricing. Best for the widest published EU GPU catalogue.
- Nscale: an AI-first cloud running hydro-powered data centres in Glomfjord, Norway (EEA), with H100, H200 and GB200/GB300-class systems sold by quote. Best for large committed training clusters.
- Verda (formerly DataCrunch, Finland): public on-demand and spot pricing for H100, H200, B200 and GB300. Best for price-sensitive training and fine-tuning with transparent rates.
- Hetzner (Germany): monthly dedicated GPU servers (NVIDIA RTX 4000 SFF Ada, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), not hourly cloud. Best for cheap, steady inference you can commit to monthly.
- IONOS (Germany, United Internet): NVIDIA H200 cloud VMs at a flat per-GPU-hour rate, EU hosting and ISO 27001. Best for regulated EU workloads that want a simple H200 rate.
- Exoscale (Austria, A1 Group): GPU families around NVIDIA A40, A30, V100 and RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell across Frankfurt, Vienna, Geneva and Zagreb. Best for compliance-heavy EU workloads that do not need H100 or H200.
- Vast.ai and RunPod (GPU marketplaces): H100 SXM and A100 by the hour at the cheapest headline rates, where European hosting, DPA coverage and uptime depend on the individual host you rent from. Best for burst and experimentation, not regulated production.

results.title: Nebius to Raise GPU Cloud Pricing Across H100, H200
results.author: MarketCatalyst Desk
highlights:
# Nebius to Raise GPU Cloud Pricing Across H100, H200, B200 and B300 Starting Oct. 1

Nebius will raise on-demand GPU cloud pricing across H100, H200, B200 and B300 starting October 1, as it scales capacity and secures financing tied to deployed GPUs.

Published Sep 17, 2026 · 4:44 PM ET · 4 min read

...

Nebius Group (NASDAQ: NBIS) is planning to raise prices on several of its on-demand GPU, CPU, and memory services starting October 1, according to a customer pricing notice reviewed by MarketCatalyst. The adjustments touch the company's most sought-after compute tiers — NVIDIA's H100, H200, B200, and B300 chips — and follow a strong second quarter shaped by rising AI Cloud demand.

...

## What's Changing

The notice lists new per-GPU-hour rates across four NVIDIA chip families, plus adjustments to underlying CPU and memory pricing:

| Hardware | New Rate | Previous Rate | Region(s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA H100 | $4.50 / GPU-hr | $3.85 / GPU-hr | eu-north1 |
| NVIDIA H200 | $5.40 / GPU-hr | $4.50 / GPU-hr | Listed European & U.S. regions |
| NVIDIA B200 | $8.50 / GPU-hr | $7.15 / GPU-hr | us-central1, me-west1 |
| NVIDIA B300 | $9.50 / GPU-hr | $7.85 / GPU-hr | uk-south1, eu-west2, us-north1 |

The increases range from roughly 15% for the H100 and H200 to about 21% for the B300, which sees the largest adjustment of the four. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU and memory rates are also moving slightly higher as part of the same notice, while Intel Ice Lake CPU pricing remains unchanged.

The bottom line

Every chip seeing a price increase is a current-generation or near-current NVIDIA accelerator used for AI training and inference, rather than older, lower-demand hardware. This pattern is consistent with a company adjusting prices where capacity is tightest, rather than where it may be trying to move idle inventory.

...

The rate changes are set to take effect October 1 across the regions listed above. Customers with existing reserved or contracted capacity commitments are typically governed by separate contract terms rather than these on-demand list prices, though the notice offers a useful signal on the broader direction of AI compute costs as capacity remains tight across the industry.

...

### When do Nebius's new GPU prices take effect?

According to a customer pricing notice, the new rates for H100, H200, B200, and B300 GPUs, along with AMD EPYC Genoa CPU and memory pricing, are set to take effect October 1.

### How much are Nebius's GPU prices increasing?

H100 pricing in eu-north1 is set to rise to $4.50 per GPU-hour from $3.85. H200 pricing is set to rise to $5.40 per GPU-hour from $4.50 across listed European and U.S. regions. B200 pricing in us-central1 and me-west1 is set to rise to $8.50 from $7.15 per GPU-hour. B300 pricing in uk-south1, eu-west2, and us-north1 is set to rise to $9.50 from $7.85 per GPU-hour.
